newsitem.title: USA: Traveling Clinton plays golf, raises campaign funds.
newsitem.headline: Traveling Clinton plays golf, raises campaign funds.

text.p: Ignoring Republican taunts to tend to budget business, President Bill Clinton played a round of golf on Sunday before helping fellow Democrats raise money for next year's congressional election campaign.

Clinton, midway through a three-day swing through the western United States, hit the links at the exclusive Hillcrest Country Club in Century City with a foursome that included Los Angeles Mayor Richard Reardon and women's tour pro Amy Alcott.
His golfing excursion, which followed breakfast at the Santa Monica beachfront home of grocery tycoon Ron Burkle, came as the final round of budget and tax talks proceeded in Washington.

Later, Clinton was to speak at a fundraising dinner sponsored by the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee. The event, unhampered by a flurry of investigations into Clinton's re-election campaign fundraising tactics, was expected to raise hundreds of thousands of dollars for next year's congressional and gubernatorial campaigns.

In an appearance on NBC-TV's Sunday talk show "Meet the Press," Senate Republican leader Trent Lott chided Clinton for being out of Washington, saying a budget deal was close but elusive and that the president needed to meet with him and House Speaker Newt Gingrich.

The White House said Clinton, who begin his trip on Saturday with an environmental meeting at Lake Tahoe, was "fully engaged" through his negotiating team, which includes Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
"At the appropriate time, he (Clinton) would be willing to get personally involved in the talks," presidential spokesman Joe Lockhart told Reuters.
Clinton aides kept reporters and photographers out of shouting and camera distance from the president during his golf game.

The White House said last week that Clinton was ready to give up his scheduled August vacation in Martha's Vineyard, Mass., to finish up the tax and spending deals. Congressional Republican leaders have said they want to complete passage of implementing legislation before the Senate and House of Representatives recess for vacation on Aug 1.
Clinton was to travel to Las Vegas on Monday to address the annual summer meeting of the nation's 50 state governors. He was to return to Washington early on Tuesday.
